ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders with significant control, and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada consolidated autonomous sanctions list, and FINTRAC/RCMP watchlists; Enhanced due diligence required for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs) under FINTRAC guidance; simplified yet mandatory verification applies for Low_Risk_Standard tier; source of funds documentation must be captured for non-arm's-length inbound transfers.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry - Corporate Online Service Centre (CORES), administered by Service Alberta, accessible at corporate-registry.alberta.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must use the 26 letters of the English alphabet and may include numerals, punctuation, and recognized corporate identifiers; NUANS name search report is mandatory and must be submitted with the articles; FTrade names and transliterations must be registered separately if non-English script is used in commerce.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may submit a revised NUANS search report with a new name; alternatively, a formal written reconsideration may be filed with the Registrar of Corporations citing distinguishing or acquired distinctiveness evidence; if the Registrar upholds the refusal, judicial review may be sought in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within 30 days of the decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is acceptable only for the statutory registered office and records address, provided a real street address within Alberta is maintained for service of process; a P.O. Box alone is prohibited; the actual double-shot PBT injection molding operation requires a physical production premises satisfying municipal zoning and fire safety bylaws.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 15–20% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months, primarily municipal fire and building safety authority visits due to plastics processing equipment; CRA compliance verification visits may occur but are not registry-mandated and follow standard risk-based assessment.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9, ss. 6(1), 15.1(1), 101, 103, 104, and 112; Corporate Names Regulation, Alta. Reg. 68/2011.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction (via the CorpReg online portal and authorized service providers)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form INC-1) endorsed with an unlimited liability provision under section 15.1(1) of the Alberta Business Corporations Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the ABCA; shares may be issued for cash, property, or past services; no escrow or trust account requirement for a non-offering Alberta ULC. Directors determine capital adequacy by resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company under the Alberta Business Corporations Act is hereby ratified; further RESOLVED, that the subscription for 1,000 common shares by the subscriber named in the Articles of Incorporation is accepted, and the consideration therefor is approved; further RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is established at 123 Corporate Plaza, Calgary, Alberta, and the registered office records are adopted; further RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until successors are elected; further RESOLVED, that the directors and officers are authorized to open bank accounts and make all ancillary filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta — CorpReg portal via a registered corporate search provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a prescribed Name Search Report for the proposed name 'Custom Mechanical Keyboard Caps ULC'; verify distinctiveness under the Alberta Corporate Names Regulation. Upon a successful search, submit a Name Reservation Request through the CorpReg desktop or web portal to reserve the name for 90 days. The corporate name must include 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', 'ULC', or the French-language equivalent 'Société à responsabilité illimitée' (S.A.R.I.).
required_dossiers: Written consent of any individual whose name appears in the proposed corporate name (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry refuses the name as not distinctive or confusingly similar, file a remedial Name Reservation Request with an alternate distinctive name within the validity period of the search report; if a name conflict is raised after reservation, the Registry will transfer the reservation to an alternate name without an additional name-search fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing Articles of Incorporation for the ULC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta — electronic submission through CorpReg or paper filing at the Registry counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Articles of Incorporation consistent with Form INC-1, inserting the unlimited liability provision under section 15.1(1) of the ABCA, the Alberta registered office address, the initial directors, and the authorized common voting share class. File the Articles through CorpReg, pay the prescribed filing fee, and obtain the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the corporate identifier. No notarization is required for a domestic Alberta ULC.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (Form INC-1) containing the unlimited liability provision
Consent of the first directors named in the Articles
Alberta physical street address for the registered office
Payment receipt for the prescribed filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a deficiency or query notice, correct and resubmit the Articles within 20 days through the CorpReg portal; corrective resubmissions are processed without an additional state fee, and the priority date restarts at the date of the clean resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance — First Board Resolutions, Share Issue, and Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Board of Directors; Corporate Registry for any later share-structure amendments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first organizational board meeting immediately after issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation; pass the pro-forma First Board Resolution adopting the registered office, accepting the share subscription, and appointing the President, Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer. Issue share certificates, prepare the register of directors, register of shareholders, and securities register, and maintain the corporate minute book at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation and corporate identifier
Certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation
Minute book containing the First Board Resolution
Registers of directors, officers, and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If officer consents or minute signatures are incomplete, re-adopt the resolution with the proper parties and re-date the minutes; if the share capital schedule is defective, file Amending Articles through CorpReg to correct the authorized capital.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence, Fire Safety, and Workplace Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary Licence and Permit Access portal (or the relevant Alberta municipality); Calgary Fire Department; Alberta Occupational Health and Safety; WCB-Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing double-shot PBT plastic injection operations, apply for the municipal manufacturing business licence at the production address; schedule a municipal building-safety inspection to verify structural load and occupancy compliance; submit a fire safety plan to the local fire prevention officer for approval; and obtain a WCB-Alberta clearance letter covering injection-molding equipment and employees. Maintain the licence and workplace safety documentation on site.
required_dossiers: Municipal business licence application and operations description
Fire safety plan and fire-code compliance statement
Building occupancy and structural load inspection certificate or lease inspection agreement
WCB-Alberta employer registration and clearance letter
Alberta OHS hazard assessment and safety policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal licence is refused or suspended, remedy by responding to the municipal licensing notice, correcting identified fire-code deficiencies, and re-inspecting; building and fire determinations may be appealed to the Safety Codes Council.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Licensing and Permitting Authority of the City of Calgary (or the applicable Alberta municipality); Alberta Environmental Protection and other safety regulatory bodies as applicable
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Alberta Municipal General Business Licence — Manufacturing and Reprocessing

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA), Environmental Assessment Division; federal triggers reviewed by Environment and Climate Change Canada
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — small-scale plastic injection molding is not listed as a mandatory EIA activity under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA), but a Category A registration may apply if wastewater discharge or air emission thresholds are exceeded
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives for fine particulate matter and total organic carbon from stack emissions; plant wastewater must meet municipal sewer discharge bylaws (e.g., City of Calgary Sewer Use Bylaw W-199); plastic waste segregation and recycling under the EPEA Waste Management Regulations

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code and Safety Codes Act; structural load inspection and occupancy permit from the municipal building safety authority; Alberta OHS workplace clearance for the injection molding facility; WCB-Alberta certificate of clearance for employer operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Agence du revenu du Canada — national tax administration; Business Registration Online (BRO) portal: https://www.canada.ca/en/services/taxes/business-taxes/business-number.html. Alberta provincial corporate income tax is administered for the Province of Alberta by the CRA under the Provincial Tax Collection Agreement; Alberta Treasury Board and Finance administers only the corporate income tax of Alberta financial institutions, which is not applicable to this manufacturing ULC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Alberta ULC: (1) incorporate under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) through the Alberta Corporate Registry, maintain an Alberta registered office and appoint at least one director (Alberta imposes no director residency requirement, no minimum capital and no non-resident ownership approval); (2) obtain the Alberta Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Access Number; (3) obtain the federal Business Number (BN) by filing Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts' online through Business Registration Online, or by phone, fax or mail; (4) activate on the BN the program accounts required for a custom-manufacturing exporter: RC (corporate income tax), RT (GST/HST) and, if employees are engaged, RP (payroll); (5) the CRA assigns a 9-digit BN with two-letter program identifiers (e.g., RC0001, RT0001); (6) file the GST/HST registration before commencing taxable activity and notify the CRA of changes of address, directors or business activity within the legislated notification periods.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation for Canadian income tax purposes: an Alberta ULC is a taxable Canadian corporation under ITA s. 89(1), resident in Canada and taxable on worldwide income at the federal general corporate rate plus Alberta provincial corporate income tax collected by the CRA. Pass_Through_Eligible for U.S. federal income tax purposes because the unlimited-liability shareholder may elect under check-the-box to treat the ULC as a disregarded entity or partnership, creating a hybrid entity; the Canadian entity-level tax status is not altered by the U.S. election.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (i) U.S. check-the-box election under Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-3 to classify the Alberta ULC as a disregarded entity (single member) or partnership (multi-member) for U.S. federal tax; (ii) fiscally transparent entity relief under Article IV(6) and (7) of the Canada-U.S. Income Tax Convention as amended by the Fifth Protocol, allowing income of the ULC to be treated as derived by its U.S. resident member where appropriate; (iii) Canadian hybrid-mismatch constraints under ITA ss. 18.2–18.4, with available elections to recognize or recharacterize hybrid mismatch payments for interest deductibility purposes; and (iv) GST/HST election under ETA s. 156 to treat supplies between closely related registrants as made for nil consideration, available where the ULC and a related registrant satisfy the closely-related test.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) imposed under the Excise Tax Act; Alberta has no provincial retail sales tax, so the applicable headline rate on supplies made in Alberta is the 5% federal GST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in total taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) made in a single calendar quarter or cumulatively over four consecutive calendar quarters; registration becomes mandatory within 30 days of exceeding the threshold (ETA s. 240).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based e-invoice acceptance for GST/HST purposes. Registrants with annual gross revenue exceeding CAD 1 million must file GST/HST returns and rebate applications electronically under ETA s. 238.02. Optional e-invoicing may follow the Pan-Canadian e-invoice standard (PEPPOL BIS) under the CRA's voluntary e-invoicing service; regardless of invoicing format, the ULC must retain full invoicing and export evidence for six years following the end of the relevant reporting period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A GST/HST registrant zero-rates double-shot PBT plastic keycaps supplied for export under ETA s. 21 where the supplier exports the goods as part of the supply, or under ETA s. 22 where a non-resident purchaser exports the goods after acquisition; the goods must actually leave Canada within a reasonable time, the supply must be made to a non-resident, and the registrant must hold sufficient books and records to link the supply to physical export and to the foreign consideration received. Related design and digital-delivery services supplied to a non-resident may separately qualify for zero-rating under the ETA's non-resident services rule where the prescribed conditions (including the non-resident status of the recipient and the absence of Canadian real-property or Canadian-delivered tangible-property connection) are satisfied.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Export Declaration — CBSA B13A (or approved electronic export report / e-manifest) filed where the value of the exported keycaps exceeds CAD 2,000 or the goods are controlled or regulated
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list identifying the non-resident consignee outside Canada, the HS classification (HS 3926.90 or HS 8473.30 as applicable) and the stated export value
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing shipment from Canada to the foreign destination, including the carrier-assigned tracking and delivery location
Carrier manifest, Canada export transaction report, or third-party logistics door-delivery record indicating the goods left Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent SWIFT/MT103 wire-conformation or payment-gateway settlement statement showing repatriation of the export proceeds to Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may audit export zero-rating claims within the 4-year normal reassessment period under ETA s. 298; if documentary proof of actual export is deficient, CRA reverses the zero-rating, assesses 5% GST on the supply, disallows related input tax credits and charges interest on the understated tax. A false statement made knowingly or in circumstances amounting to gross negligence triggers a penalty equal to the greater of CAD 100 and 25% of the tax understated under ETA s. 285, and wilful evasion is prosecutable under ETA s. 327 with substantial fines and imprisonment. Goods diverted back into Canada, or export proceeds not received from the foreign purchaser within the 180-day tax-control benchmark, cause retrospective clawback of the zero-rating and require the ULC to self-assess GST; note that Canada imposes no exchange-control statute fixing a 180-day repatriation deadline, but the 180-day benchmark is applied here as internal transfer-pricing and zero-rating substantiation policy.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BOC); foreign exchange policy is coordinated with the Department of Finance Canada and OSFI; BOC does not operate exchange controls or license foreign-exchange dealers for internal convertibility purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility. Non-residents may freely repatriate equity contributions and trade proceeds, but dividends and deemed distributions from an Alberta ULC are subject to Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act, generally 25% unless reduced by an applicable income tax treaty (e.g., 15% under Canada-China DTA). No prior administrative approval is required for profit remittance; the Ministry of Finance does not impose material quantitative limits on foreign exchange transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion ratio exists. Export receipts from double-shot PBT keycap sales may be retained in any foreign currency. FinTRAC EFT and large cash transaction reporting obligations apply if any single transaction or series of transactions in a 24-hour period exceeds CAD 10,000, or if the physical cross-border movement of such receipts exceeds CAD 10,000.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with material legal constraints. Canada does not issue dedicated fintech EMI (Electronic Money Institution) licenses similar to the EEA regime. Offshore EMIs such as Wise and Revolut Business may provide workplace and float accounts only via a sponsor bank holding Canadian deposits, and they are not CDIC-insured. For an Alberta ULC requiring capital escrow and commercial-lending-style treasury clearing, these EMIs are viable as receiving or payout payment rails (notably in CAD/USD), but they are not appropriate for statutory capital escrow, ULC statutory filings, or fully segregated multi-currency clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under FINTRAC and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, a Canadian bank must verify the identity of at least two directors of the corporate customer using primary documents. Remote video KYC is generally accepted by Schedule I banks if the director presents a valid passport and completes a secure biometric check, and the bank requires no physical branch presence for ordinary operational accounts. However, for a Capital Escrow Account involving the initial equity injection for an Alberta ULC, most banks will require a Canadian-processed notarized corporate certificate, the Certificate of Incumbency, and a live video interview with the ultimate beneficial owner and at least one director; physical appearance at a branch is not legally mandated but may be imposed by business risk appetite.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership with a non-resident parent corporation; FATCA/CRS classification as a ULC considered fiscally transparent in the U.S. but opaque in Canada.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organizational chart executed by corporate counsel; Alberta Registry Certificate of Search; Certificate of Officers and Directors; ULC opt-in pass-through election (Form T3100 and related Alberta corporate ruling); CRS self-certification forms; shareholder registry with each UBO's name, address, and tax ID; three-month source-of-funds bank statements from the parent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce revenue from Shopify Payments and Stripe is high-volume and low-value with rapid settlement timing, creating inconsistency between declared ISIC scope 3240 and average invoice size.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed payment processor settlement reconciliation; monthly Amazon/Shopify business reports identifying the PBT double-shot keycap SKUs; the corporate website and advertising landing pages; a summary of historical credit-card refunds and chargebacks; supplier purchase orders and shipping receipts; annual audited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shares held by a corporate guarantor with no clear source of wealth; capital injection from a jurisdiction without a Canada-Jurisdiction tax treaty or with FATF-identified deficiencies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of the ultimate beneficial owner's notarized source-of-wealth statement; professional tax references; evidence of independent compressible assets; completed FINTRAC large-size transaction remittance form; an AML legal opinion describing the ULC capital contribution as an ordinary equity step; a sworn declaration of the shareholders' list.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The ULC shall receive the capital injection via SWIFT MT103. The inbound wire must identify the beneficiary bank under Field 57A and beneficiary party under Field 59. The Ordered Party field is the parent entity's issuing bank. In Field 70, the payment narrative must state '/EQIC/ EQUITY CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION FOR ULC CORPORATE TREASURY' and the exact ULC certificate number to ensure no conversion to debt. As there is no Canadian FX control, no pre-approval is required from BOC, but the bank must report the transfer to FinTRAC if the value is CAD 100,000 or above under the EFT report requirement. For any trade-related capital contribution arising from unpaid share capital, the company must attach a notarized paid-in capital resolution to the bank signatory form.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Direct trade settlements to Chinese keycap suppliers shall be routed via SWIFT MT103 (bank-to-bank) using the supplier's Chinese-issued USD or RMB account. For first-time suppliers with an invoice above USD 50,000, a Commercial Letter of Credit (form MT700) is recommended, backed by a pro-forma invoice, bill of lading, and inspection certificate; for established suppliers, D/P (Documents against Payment) via the sending bank's correspondent corridor is permitted. USD payments will clear over the U.S. correspondent Fedwire instead of Canada's Lynx real-time rail; CAD payments through Lynx are not economical for cross-border settlement. All disbursements to third-party vendors must include the ISIC/NAICS reference code 334118 to remain consistent with the declared business scope, and must comply with OFAC/sanctions screening by the Canadian bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla foreign exchange forwards (10-day to 24-month tenor) with Schedule I dealers, covering USD/CAD, RMB/CAD, and EUR/CAD exposures; governed by ISDA 1992 and 2002 Master Agreement with CSA collateral.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for the offshore RMB (CNH) leg to manage large keycap inventory purchases where the Chinese supplier imposes RMB settlement but the ULC has CAD or USD cash flows; NDF fixing generally references the offshore RMB central parity (CNH) as published by the China Foreign Exchange Trade System.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for intercompany loans between the ULC and its foreign parent, used to align cashflow hedges of the principal and coupon payments without triggering bankable debt exposure; additionally, foreign exchange rollover swaps are permissible for next-value-date liquidity adjustment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Business Corporations Act, Alberta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the corporation's anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 50 late filing fee applied immediately; continued non-filing for two or more years may result in administrative dissolution of the corporation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Federal + Alberta Provincial)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 6 months after fiscal year end; balance due date is 2 months after year end for non-CCPCs and 3 months for CCPCs claiming small business deduction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty: 5% of balance owing plus 1% per full month late, up to 12 months; repeated failure can lead to CRA enforcement action and prosecution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (if annual remittance filer)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 3 months after fiscal year end for annual GST/HST filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 6% of the amount due plus 2% per full month late (subject to annual filer threshold); interest charged on overdue amounts

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit threshold based on revenue or assets for non-distributing Alberta private corporations. An independent auditor is required only if corporation is a reporting issuer or distributing corporation; otherwise shareholders may waive auditor appointment by unanimous resolution. A ULC can rely on unanimous consent to avoid mandatory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable entities; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private enterprises, including ULCs, unless CRA or external lenders require IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta ABCA does not currently mandate a standalone annual UBO confirmation filing. For shareholding transfers, the corporation must update the Register of Members and record the transfer date, number of shares, and parties within a reasonable time. A voluntary register of individuals with significant control (ISC) may be maintained and confirmed annually for good governance; no public provincial filing is required for a private ULC.
